events.title: Henry the Lion wins the dispute over Munich at Augsburg
events.description: At Augsburg, a dispute between Duke Henry the Lion and Bishop Otto of Freising was settled in Henry's favour; the ruling named the place as forum apud Munichen. Henry had to pay the bishop a third of his income.
events.html: At Augsburg, a dispute between Duke Henry the Lion and Bishop Otto of Freising was settled in Henry's favour; the ruling named the place as forum apud Munichen. Henry had to pay the bishop a third of his income.

events.title: Prince Louis of France takes Winchester in the First Barons' War
events.description: Prince Louis of France, who had invaded England at the invitation of rebel barons, captured Winchester, abandoned by King John. After John's death in October, many barons deserted Louis for John's young son Henry III.
events.html: Prince Louis of France, who had invaded England at the invitation of rebel barons, captured Winchester, abandoned by King John. After John's death in October, many barons deserted Louis for John's young son Henry III.

events.title: The exiled Song court crowns Emperor Duanzong in Fuzhou
events.description: In exile in Fuzhou from the advancing Mongols, the remnants of the Song court crowned Zhao Shi as Emperor Duanzong, the penultimate emperor of the Southern Song. Under Kublai Khan the Mongols completed their conquest of the Song in 1279.
events.html: In exile in Fuzhou from the advancing Mongols, the remnants of the Song court crowned Zhao Shi as Emperor Duanzong, the penultimate emperor of the Southern Song. Under Kublai Khan the Mongols completed their conquest of the Song in 1279.

events.title: Rebels storm the Tower of London in the Peasants' Revolt
events.description: Rebels of the Peasants' Revolt stormed the Tower of London and killed Simon Sudbury, Archbishop of Canterbury and Lord Chancellor, and Robert Hales, Lord High Treasurer. The same day the young Richard II met the rebels and promised reforms.
events.html: Rebels of the Peasants' Revolt stormed the Tower of London and killed Simon Sudbury, Archbishop of Canterbury and Lord Chancellor, and Robert Hales, Lord High Treasurer. The same day the young Richard II met the rebels and promised reforms.

events.title: New Model Army defeats Charles I at Naseby
events.description: Fairfax and Cromwell's New Model Army destroyed the main royalist army in Northamptonshire. Captured royal letters damaged the king's cause, and the First Civil War was effectively decided.
events.html: Fairfax and Cromwell's New Model Army destroyed the main royalist army in Northamptonshire. Captured royal letters damaged the king's cause, and the First Civil War was effectively decided.

events.title: Congress adopts the Stars and Stripes
events.description: The Flag Resolution called for thirteen stripes, red and white, and thirteen white stars on a blue field. The anniversary is celebrated in the US as Flag Day.
events.html: The Flag Resolution called for thirteen stripes, red and white, and thirteen white stars on a blue field. The anniversary is celebrated in the US as Flag Day.

events.title: Napoleon wins at Marengo
events.description: Near defeat by the Austrians, Napoleon was saved by Desaix's arriving division, and the battle turned. The victory secured northern Italy and his position as First Consul.
events.html: Near defeat by the Austrians, Napoleon was saved by Desaix's arriving division, and the battle turned. The victory secured northern Italy and his position as First Consul.

events.title: German troops enter Paris
events.description: The Wehrmacht marched into the French capital, which had been declared an open city. France signed an armistice eight days later.
events.html: The Wehrmacht marched into the French capital, which had been declared an open city. France signed an armistice eight days later.

events.title: Argentine forces surrender at Port Stanley
events.description: The surrender ended the 74-day Falklands War, in which 649 Argentine and 255 British service personnel died. Argentina's military junta fell soon after.
events.html: The surrender ended the 74-day Falklands War, in which 649 Argentine and 255 British service personnel died. Argentina's military junta fell soon after.
